en: Itivuttaka 73:
Tikanipāta, Tatiyavagga (The Third Chapter)
The More Peaceful Discourse.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
“Monks, the formless is more peaceful than forms; cessation is more peaceful than the formless.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“And those beings who have gone to the realm of form...”
And those who abide in the formless realms,
not understanding cessation,
are subject to renewed existence.
Those who, having fully understood forms,
do not settle upon the formless,
and who are liberated in cessation—
Those people have escaped from death;
having touched with their own bodies the Deathless element,
which is free from acquisitions.
Having realized the relinquishing of acquisitions,
the Tathāgata, the Perfectly Enlightened One, who is free from taints, teaches.
“The sorrowless, stainless state.
This meaning was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fourth [sutta].
